body:
The frozen worker06 source case retains `Na2MnO4·2H2O` in JCM1357, and the current primary JCM recipe independently prints that exact formula in its Trace Metal Mix A5 table. This is not an importer-only typo that can safely be normalized to sodium molybdate: Mn and Mo denote different elements.

Primary source: https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1357 (Trace Metal Mix A5 table, 0.39 g). Worker evidence: `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-06/research-a/captures/53c817edb16209b2.raw`, recorded in `A-E-CAPTURE-106`. Independent root review read the source table and retained the hold.

Frozen occurrence: `CultureMech:015838:ingredients/14`; source case `CM_NAME:0de1cd6a8da27db3330c739fddfbd28decf8c771a01ff97a40179faca8894f95`. This issue describes the frozen campaign case and current primary source, not an assertion about a later CultureMech export. No maintained source, ontology assignment or downstream hold was changed.

Follow-up: obtain an authoritative JCM1357 correction, original reagent specification or source revision identifying whether the printed manganese formula or a molybdenum reagent was intended, including hydration and amount. Then review the exact source occurrence and distinct ingredient identity. Until that evidence exists, preserve the printed formula and withhold inferred molybdate/manganate equivalence.

Deduplication: searched the complete retained live MIM issue inventory and a fresh all-state search for1357; no matching issue was returned. The broader source-release backlog and stock-completeness issues do not resolve this element-level contradiction.
title: Resolve JCM1357 Na2MnO4·2H2O before assigning a molybdate identity

body:
Review findings on #746 (read-only pass).

1. **Stale `object_label` on a registry row.** `MIM:Anisodamine_Hydrobromide` had its `subject_label` corrected to `Anisodamine Hydrobromide` on all three rows, and the `cas:` row was rewritten, but the `kgmicrobe.compound:anisodamine_hydrobromide` row still carries `object_label = "Anisodamine Hydrobromide ()"`, the old label with the ingest artefact. Registry rows take the record's `preferred_term` as their object label; the finish step must rewrite it for a relabelled subject.

2. **Old-term synonyms still published through `other`.** When the own-identifier row's object moves to a different term (ammonium molybdate CHEBI:91249 → CHEBI:86244, acridine orange, 4-hydroxynonenal, aluminium sulfate, bisabolene, ferulate), `reconcile_sssom` rewrites the object but leaves `other` as the enrichment builder filled it for the *old* term. `MIM:Ammonium_Molybdate_Tetrahydrate → CHEBI:86244` therefore still lists `Diammonium molybdate`, a name of the orthomolybdate the row just left. Under Section 1 a synonym channel token must name the row's substance; the finish step should drop every `other` token that is a name of the old term and not of the new one (and not a resolving synonym on the record).

Both are `--finish-sssom` defects in `scripts/apply_312_batch2.py`; fix there and regenerate the receipt/chain.
title: Batch-2 finish step leaves the old identity's traces on sibling rows: stale object_label on a relabelled subject's registry row, old-term synonyms in other

body:
`UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` on `main` (1742bfd4) has 33 rows that are REJECTED with an empty `chebi_id`, `kg_microbe_node_id` and `mim_id`. They cover 3,378 recipe occurrences, and all 33 were MAPPED at 48408270 (#731, 2026-09-22).

| snapshot | REJECTED rows with no identity | occurrences |
|---|---:|---:|
| 48408270 (#731, 2026-09-22) | 0 | 0 |
| a8b26f00 (#754, 2026-09-25) | 47 | 9,386 |
| 6643131b (#802, 2026-10-05) | 47 | 9,391 |
| 1742bfd4 (#863, 2026-10-12) | 33 | 3,378 |

kg-microbe's consolidator skips REJECTED rows (`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py:1604-1606` at kg-microbe 1408e7099). MIM therefore supplies no identity for these labels. I did not check what kg-microbe falls back to.

## Cause

claw's unified builder finds a merge tombstone's target in `_mim_merge_target` (`scripts/build_unified_ingredient_mapping.py:129-140` at the pinned claw a5d56296):

```python
for event in reversed(data.get('curation_history', []) or []):
    if event.get('action') in MIM_MERGE_ACTIONS:
        return (data.get('identifier') or '').strip()
    if event.get('new_status') == 'REJECTED':
        return ''
```

The builder walks the history backwards and stops at the first event with `new_status: REJECTED`. Nine tombstones later gained a bookkeeping event recorded as REJECTED → REJECTED, so the walk stops before it reaches the merge:

| tombstone | identifier | blocking event |
|---|---|---|
| `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` | CHEBI:53503 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na2moo42h2o` | CHEBI:75213 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Calcium_Chloride` | CHEBI:3312 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Sodium_Citrate` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na-glutamate` | CHEBI:64243 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` | CHEBI:86345 | CORRECTED (#739) |
| `Nah2po4h2o` | CHEBI:114249 | CORRECTED (#755) |
| `Cinnamic_Acid` | CHEBI:35697 | CORRECTED (#755); none of the 33 rows |

The corpus has 81 REJECTED records. Of these, 13 set `representative:`, 51 resolve through their merge event, these 9 resolve to nothing, and 8 have no merge event. The #755 CORRECTED events were written "so the merged name is credited to the live record". In the unified build they have the opposite effect.

## Rows affected

| labels | occurrences | identity at 48408270 | answer the records support now |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` | 2,317 | CHEBI:53503 cobalt chloride hexahydrate | same |
| 7 other CoCl2·6H2O spellings | 358 | CHEBI:35696 cobalt dichloride (anhydrous) | CHEBI:53503 |
| 6 Na2MoO4·2H2O spellings | 412 | CHEBI:75213 sodium molybdate dihydrate | same |
| 5 Na2MoO4·H2O spellings | 8 | CHEBI:75215 sodium molybdate (anhydrous) | none: no monohydrate record |
| `Sodium citrate`, `Sodium Citrate`, `sodium citrate` | 94 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | contested, see below |
| `Calcium chloride`, `calcium chloride` | 82 | CHEBI:86158 calcium chloride dihydrate | CHEBI:3312 (live `CaCl2` lists `Calcium chloride`) |
| `Calcium Chloride` | 15 | CHEBI:3312 calcium dichloride | same |
| `Trisodium citrate x 2 H2O`, `Trisodium citrate・2H2O` | 77 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | CHEBI:32142 sodium citrate dihydrate |
| `Trisodium citrate・3H2O`, `Trisodium citrate x 3 H2O` | 3 | CHEBI:53258 | none: no record for that form |
| `NaH2PO4•H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:37585 sodium dihydrogenphosphate (anhydrous) | CHEBI:114249 monohydrate |
| `MgCl2x 6 H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:86345 magnesium dichloride hexahydrate | same |
| `MgCl2 x 7H2O` | 2 | CHEBI:6636 magnesium dichloride (anhydrous) | kgmicrobe.compound:mgcl2_x_7_h2o |
| `Na-glutamate` | 2 | CHEBI:64220 monosodium glutamate | CHEBI:64243 monosodium L-glutamate |

- **Rows that lost an identity the records still support:** 2,748 occurrences in the "same" rows, mostly `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` (2,317) and the sodium molybdate dihydrate spellings (412).
- **Rows that had a wrong form at 48408270:** 534 occurrences. These should have been corrected, not dropped.
- **Contested labels (94 occurrences):** for the sodium citrate names, live `Trisodium citrate` (CHEBI:53258) lists `Sodium citrate`, while live `Na3-citrate x 2 H2O` (CHEBI:32142, the dihydrate) lists `Sodium Citrate`.
- **`Na-glutamate` (2 occurrences):** it had generic monosodium glutamate, where MIM now holds the L-form.

## Fix

Setting `representative:` on the nine tombstones, as 13 others already do, would make claw resolve them again. That step alone is not safe. Several tombstones still carry names of other forms as publishable synonyms, and a restored merge target would publish those names under the wrong form:

- `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): `CoCl2 x 2 H2O` and `CoCl2 x 4 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). Both forms have had their own records since #863.
- `Na2moo42h2o` (dihydrate): four monohydrate spellings (HYDRATE_FORM): `Na2MoO4 . H2O`, `Na2MoO4 · H2O`, `Na2MoO4.H2O` and `Na2MoO4xH2O`.
- `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): five spellings, `MgCl2 x 7 H2O`, `MgCl2 x 7H2O`, `MgCl2x7H2O`, `MgCl2  x 7 H2O` and `MgCl2  x 76 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` (dihydrate): `Trisodium citrate·3H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Calcium_Chloride` (anhydrous): `CaCl22H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). #757 retyped two other dihydrate spellings but not this one.
- `Na-glutamate` (monosodium L-glutamate): `(2S)-2-aminopentanedioate` and `L-glutamic acid dianion` (EXACT_SYNONYM). Both are names of the anion.
- `Sodium_Citrate` (dihydrate CHEBI:32142): its preferred term `Sodium Citrate` is a generic name, and its synonym `Na2citrate` names disodium citrate.

Suggested order:

1. Retype those names as REJECTED_LABEL, or move each to the record for its form, with curation events.
2. Set `representative:` on the nine tombstones. If review pins (#740, #745) block these edits, change claw instead: when looking for the merge, skip events whose `previous_status` is already REJECTED.
3. Rebuild with `just rebuild-unified`. Check that the 33 rows come back, except the 11 occurrences whose form has no record.
4. Add a gate. `check-unified-freshness` and `check-unified-rejections` both pass on the current snapshot. Either of these checks would have caught this:
   - every merge tombstone carries `representative:`;
   - no REJECTED row without an identity has a tombstone's name as its label.

Related:
- #878 covers MAPPED labels that sit on a different hydrate.
- #877 is the membership rebuild. It reports that CultureMech#591 now refuses tombstone redirects across hydrates on CultureMech's side.

## Correction to #863

#863's description calls rows like these "merged-tombstone answers that the reviewed builder withholds (MIM #811, #816)". Nothing is withheld on purpose: the builder loses the merge target as described above, and neither #811 nor #816 covers that.
title: 33 unified rows (3,378 recipe occurrences) lost their identity: nine merge tombstones no longer resolve to their merge target

body:
Found while cross-checking CultureBotAI/CultureMech#272.

`docs/data/label_index.csv` resolves the label **`Na2MoO4·2H2O`** to **`CHEBI:75215`** — *sodium molybdate (anhydrous)* — because that string is carried as a **synonym on the `Na2MoO4` record**.

But MIM also has a dedicated record for that exact label, and it points at the dihydrate:

    label_index:  Na2MoO4·2H2O  -> CHEBI:75215  via synonym on record `Na2MoO4`  (MAPPED)
    the record:   Na2MoO4·2H2O  -> CHEBI:75213  sodium molybdate dihydrate       (REJECTED, merged in #341)

So a consumer joining on the label gets the **anhydrous** term, even though MIM's own curation concluded the dihydrate. CultureMech#272 independently picks `CHEBI:75213`, and is right.

## The general shape

A synonym on record A can name the same string as record B's `preferred_term`. When A is live and B is a tombstone, `label_index` resolves the string via A — silently preferring a synonym match on one record over a preferred-term match on another.

Here that is actively wrong because the synonym crosses a hydration boundary: `Na2MoO4·2H2O` should never resolve to an anhydrous term, whichever record carries it.

## Options

1. **Prefer `preferred_term` matches over `synonym` matches** when both exist for a string — `label_index` already records `match_type`, so the precedence is expressible and cheap.
2. **Follow tombstones**: when the preferred-term match is REJECTED, resolve to its merge target (`identifier` already points there) rather than falling back to a synonym on a different record.
3. **Remove hydration-crossing synonyms**: `Na2MoO4·2H2O` should arguably not be a synonym of `Na2MoO4` at all, since they are different substances. Worth auditing for other hydrate strings carried as synonyms of their anhydrous parent.

(1) and (2) are index-level and fix the class; (3) is data-level and fixes instances. They are not exclusive.

Related: #370 (collection decides publication), #360 (tombstones keep an `ontology_id` they no longer assert) — all three are cases where a tombstone or an index rule routes a lookup somewhere the curation did not intend.
title: A hydrate label can resolve through a synonym to the anhydrous record's term
